sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Haywood County?
sections.html:
Two offices at the Historic Haywood Courthouse in Waynesville split the work: the Tax Assessor's Office values property, and Tax Collections bills and takes payment. The assessor is at 215 N. Main Street, Suite 220 and Tax Collections is at Suite 224 of the same address.

Collections answers at 828-452-6643, and the assessor's line for reappraisal questions is 828-452-6734.

A Haywood bill can include more than a county rate. The county collects for 22 fire districts, 10 road maintenance districts and one sanitation district, and owners of improved property, including manufactured homes and campers, pay a landfill fee on top.

The county covers 553.56 square miles of land and had an estimated 63,369 residents on July 1, 2025, up 2.1% from the 2020 base. The average worker spends 23.8 minutes getting to work, and the Census Bureau counted 4,981 veterans for 2020-2024, which is relevant because the disabled veteran exclusion has no age or income limit.

sections.h2: When are Haywood County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Bills go out in late August or early September, taxes are due in September, and they stay interest-free through January 5. After that the county adds 2% and then another three-quarters of one percent on the first day of each month until the bill is paid.

Haywood County tax dates from the county's own pages
DateWhat happens
January 1Ownership of real property is fixed for the tax year
Late August to early SeptemberBills mailed to owners
SeptemberTaxes due
January 5Last day without interest
After January 52% interest, then 3/4% on the first of each month
MarchUnpaid real estate taxes advertised with a fee added

Sources: Haywood County Office of Tax Collections FAQ and Tax Collections.

An owner who cannot pay in full by January 5 may arrange a set monthly amount by calling Collections. The state rule for the due date and interest is in G.S. 105-360.

sections.h2: How can I pay a Haywood County tax bill?
sections.html:
The county takes payment online, by phone, by mail, through a dropbox at the Historic Courthouse, or in cash at the Tax Collections office. The processor charges a 3% fee on card payments, 2% on e-checks, and 3% for a card payment by phone at 1-877-729-8290, and the county receives none of it.

  • Checks and money orders can go in the dropbox in front of the courthouse, but no cash.
  • Mailed payments go to the address on the bill. The county changed its lockbox address, and a payment returned by the post office can be resent to the Waynesville address in the original envelope, with the original postmark honored.
  • The county does not send tax bills to a lender or escrow company, so an owner whose lender pays the tax should pass a copy of the bill to that lender.

sections.h2: Why was the Haywood County revaluation moved to 2027?
sections.html:
Haywood County postponed its reappraisal from 2025 to January 1, 2027 because of Hurricane Helene damage, after working with the state to confirm the delay was allowed. The county announced the change on November 5, 2024.

Under that plan, 2025 values stayed the same for most parcels unless a property changed through additions, updates, new construction or flood damage. The 2027 values will reflect market conditions at that time, so a house in Waynesville or Maggie Valley may carry a very different assessed value after the reset.

Commissioners held a public hearing on October 19, 2026 on the schedule of values, standards and rules for the 2027 reappraisal, and a copy of the schedules is kept at the Tax Assessor's Office on the second floor for public inspection. State law requires reappraisal at least every eighth year, as set out in G.S. 105-286.

sections.h2: How do I report storm damage or appeal a Haywood County value?
sections.html:
Damage reports go to the Tax Assessor's Office on a Damage Report Form, and the county takes them in person, by mail or by email to personalproperty@haywoodcountync.gov. A seller whose house was flooded should file one so the assessed value reflects the condition on the ground.

Value appeals go to the Board of Equalization and Review. Haywood's board has five appointed members plus one alternate, serves one-year terms, and meets as needed on a schedule set by the Tax Assessor. It hears appeals on the value of real property for the tax year.

  • Under G.S. 105-322, a hearing request must come before the board adjourns.
  • The board mails its decision within 30 days after adjournment.
  • The next step, an appeal to the Property Tax Commission, is due within 30 days after the board mails its notice.

sections.h2: What property tax relief can a Haywood County homeowner claim?
sections.html:
Haywood County has an older population, with 28.2% of residents 65 or over, so the state's elderly and disabled programs matter here. Owners apply on Form AV-9 with the county tax assessor, and each owner can receive benefit from only one of the three programs.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: the greater of $25,000 or 50% of appraised value of a permanent residence, with a 2026 income limit of $38,800.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: the first $45,000 of appraised value, with no age or income limit.
  • Circuit breaker: tax limited to 4.0% of income at or below the limit and 5.0% above it, up to $58,200, for owners who have lived in the home at least five years.

The forms are due in the listing period but accepted through June 1. Taxes deferred under the circuit breaker become due when the home is transferred, which is a closing item on a sale.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Haywood County property tax, and what about a sale?
sections.html:
Foreclosure can start any day after January 5 of the collection year, though the county says it forecloses only when an owner does not respond or breaks a payment arrangement. Before that, the collector can attach bank accounts, garnish wages or rents, or levy on personal property.

The county uses two routes. In an in-rem foreclosure under G.S. 105-375, the Tax Department and County Attorney handle everything, and in a mortgage-style case under G.S. 105-374 an outside attorney does. Sales are public auctions in front of the Haywood County Justice Center, as is and without warranty, with a 20% deposit and a balance due at the end of the 10-day period and confirmation. Upset bids must exceed the last bid by 5%, at least $750, and are filed with the Clerk of Superior Court.

A sale does not close out the year's bill. The county says ownership is fixed on January 1 and a mid-year transfer does not relieve the seller, so the payoff is settled at closing. County data to keep in mind: 36,637 housing units, 74.9% owner-occupied, a median owner-occupied value of $279,200, median household income of $61,912 and 514 building permits in 2025 (Census QuickFacts).

faqs.q: When does interest start on Haywood County property tax?
faqs.a: After January 5. The county adds 2% then, and a further three-quarters of one percent on the first day of every month until the bill is paid.

faqs.q: Does Haywood County sell tax lien certificates?
faqs.a: No. The county's foreclosure page says North Carolina does not sell tax liens or tax certificates over the counter, and paying someone else's delinquent bill does not transfer ownership.

faqs.q: When is the Haywood County revaluation?
faqs.a: January 1, 2027. The county moved it from 2025 after Hurricane Helene, and 2025 values stayed the same for most properties unless something about the property changed.

faqs.q: I sold my Haywood County house, so why did I get the tax bill?
faqs.a: Because ownership of real property is set as of January 1 of the tax year, and a transfer during the year does not remove the seller's liability. Settle the year's tax at closing.

faqs.q: Where do I send storm damage reports in Haywood County?
faqs.a: To the Tax Assessor's Office at 215 N. Main Street, Suite 220, Waynesville, NC 28786, or by email to personalproperty@haywoodcountync.gov, using the Damage Report Form.
